claim: Woods's three adaptive-breakdown patterns (decompensation, working at cross purposes, stuck in outdated behaviour) are descriptive case patterns from NASA, healthcare and firefighting. No rates or controlled tests exist for them.
agent_test: Label stuck-run traces from our own logs with the three patterns and count how often each occurs, before building anything.

claim: The empirical base for resilience engineering as a safety intervention is thin: reviews find mostly qualitative work, empirical studies only from about 2015, and a critic says no peer-reviewed proof of improved outcomes.
agent_test: Do not import RE interventions on authority; admit any element only if it wins at equal tokens.
audit_note: Cooper paper is Safety Science (DOI 2020.105047), not 2022 as labelled; Herrera says empirical RE emerged around 2015.

claim: The only quantitative test of graceful extensibility theory is one train-introduction case: 21 of 24 sub-patterns matched, 176 coded items, one coder. This is pattern matching on a failure case, not a test.
agent_test: None for the agent; treat the theory as vocabulary, not a validated model.

claim: Success rate hides recovery behaviour. In embodied LLM agents Reflexion (56.3% success) and CoPAL (55.8%) differ 4.8 times in recovery cost (57.3 vs 11.9). Recovery cost rises with perturbation intensity (Spearman 0.82).
agent_test: Log recovery cost (extra steps and tokens after a failed check) beside accuracy for plain vs scaffold arms at equal tokens.

claim: Resilience aspects trade off: a fix targeting graceful extensibility raised recovery cost from 36.70 to 99.59 (+171%), while a rebound fix cut it from 59.11 to 33.73.
agent_test: Whenever a scaffold element widens the range of problems handled, also measure cost per recovery; check the element does not inflate it.

claim: LLM agents that can solve a task often do not solve it consistently across repeated trials: tau-bench gpt-4o pass^1 61.2 (retail) and pass^8 below 25%; outcome consistency low across 15 models; multi-turn runs show unreliability up 112%.
agent_test: Report pass^k, not only pass@1, for plain vs scaffold. A scaffold earns its place if pass^k rises at equal tokens.

claim: Most multi-turn loss is unreliability, not lost ability: 39% average drop over 200k+ simulated conversations, aptitude loss about 15%, concatenated instructions keep 95.1% of full-prompt score.
agent_test: Test S1 input hygiene: restate the full task in one block each round versus incremental feedback turns.

claim: Without an external signal, intrinsic self-correction does not help older models (GPT-3.5 CommonSenseQA 75.8 to 38.1; GPT-4 GSM8K 95.5 to 91.5 to 89.0). Newer models gain little (Claude Opus 4.6 +0.6 pp; several lost accuracy). Oracle or verify-first feedback helps.
agent_test: Compare S5 revise (failing output shown, located by code) versus a blind 'review your answer' pass at equal tokens.
audit_note: The 'Claude Opus 4.6 +0.6 pp' figure appears in none of the opened sources (Huang 2024, 2601.00828, 2602.02416, MatSciBench); the rest of the claim matches.

claim: Multi-agent debate did not beat self-consistency at equal numbers of responses (GSM8K, GPT-3.5: debate 83.2 at 6 and 83.0 at 9 vs self-consistency 85.3 and 88.2).
agent_test: Already covered by G9; only replicate on a current model.

claim: Repetition and loops are a leading failure class: MAST step repetition 15.7% and unaware of termination 12.4% of traces; LoopBench worst model 62.0% loop rate; agents repeat identical tool calls; strong models do not reliably change course after 3 or 6 failed repeats (MIRAGE utility 0.57-0.63). In the current MAST-Data release (1642 traces) step repetition is on 40.4% of traces; the paper's 15.7% is version-dependent.
agent_test: Measure how often the S6 impasse trigger (same error twice) fires and whether the chosen operator changes the output, on plain vs scaffold.
audit_note: Recounted MAST-Data myself: 1642 traces, step repetition on 664 (40.4%), 1237 with a failure mode; LoopBench 62.00%, MAST 15.7%/12.4% match.

claim: Verification gaps are a major failure share in multi-agent systems (21.3% or 23.5% depending on the figure in MAST; incorrect verification 9.1%, none 8.2%, premature termination 6.2%). Adding a high-level objective check gave +15.6% on ProgramDev. Recount of the released data: category shares 37.0/33.3/29.9 (spec/inter-agent/verification) by mode; the paper's two splits are not reproduced.
agent_test: Add or remove a final objective-level S8 check at equal tokens; count caught wrong answers.

claim: Simple prompt-level or protocol fixes give only partial recovery: MAST role-spec change +9.4%; Laban RECAP and SNOWBALL stayed below the single-turn score.
agent_test: Treat any prompt-only patch as unproven until it beats plain at equal tokens.

claim: Loop monitors are contested: an LLM monitor cut repetition 52% on one task but averaged +0.014 +/- 0.723 over tasks and did nothing for 1B-1.5B models; a hidden-state CUSUM detector found loop onset early (rate 0.64-0.76, false positives 0.24-0.34) but needs open weights.
agent_test: Code-side loop detection (repeated output hashes) versus an LLM monitor at equal tokens. Prefer code, per G5.

claim: A learn-from-incident loop can cut repeat incidents: AIR rules cut incidents 54 to 6 to 0 over three rounds (code agent); letting the agent invent its own remediation dropped success from 92.3% to 81.0% (embodied) and 97.7% to 76.6% (computer use). Only the authors' own task sets. Added: lessons written by the agent did not beat the raw failed transcript (repair agent, 75 bugs, lesson minus transcript -1.7 [-8.7,+4.9]); unverified lessons stored the agent's own errors 11 to 22% of the time (EDV); held-out transfer of a verified playbook shown once (Sentry).
agent_test: Compare S9 lesson lines (written, then reused) against no memory on a held-out set of the same problem classes.

claim: Recovery time and recovery quality are not the same: MTTR-A gives median recovery 6.21 s over 200 semi-simulated runs, but measures speed, not correctness.
agent_test: Do not adopt a time metric; use recovery cost in tokens plus final correctness.

claim: In multi-agent setups with random injected failures, more agents and links raised resilience, but cost rises too and failures were random rather than cognitive. A 2024 commons-harvest study found GPT-4 agents adapted where PPO agents did not.
agent_test: Not applicable to a single agent; against G4 samples are not independent. Only the cost of redundancy matters.

claim: Tool-fault and format robustness is near ceiling for most current agents; harmless prompt paraphrase is the main differentiator.
agent_test: Test the scaffold against paraphrased task statements (3 paraphrases each); check answer agreement.

claim: Safety-critical concepts of drift and loss of buffers (Rasmussen, Cook and Rasmussen, Westrum) are conceptual models with no tested prediction in the sources opened.
agent_test: A long-run agent could be checked for drift (rising steps or tokens per solved item); no direct test.

claim: Pre-launch simulation can surface latent threats: 37 latent safety threats in 24 simulation sessions at one hospital (no control).
agent_test: A pre-mortem pass is tested in other documents; skip unless gaps appear.

claim: No LLM study found that directly tests Woods's four-potentials or patterns framework with a controlled comparison; the only direct applications are one embodied-agent preprint (metrics defined by authors) and a conceptual FRAM/STPA analysis of a coding agent.
agent_test: N/A. Any claim of benefit from resilience framing is untested for LLMs.
audit_note: Absence claim ('no LLM study found') is limited to the researcher's search; the two cited applications match their abstracts.

claim: Blind self-review harms correct answers: single self-verification breaks 10.9% of correct answers and fixes 6.2% of wrong ones; four of five non-thinking models lose accuracy (net -2.1%, 342 worsened vs 233 improved), mostly by inventing a fault (69.6%). Locating the first wrong step plus a confidence exit gave net +3.9%; without the exit -49.3%. No frontier reasoning model tested in this mode in the sources opened.
agent_test: Compare blind S5 against located-failure S5 with a stop rule on the nano loop, counting correct-to-wrong and wrong-to-correct flips.

claim: Writing a lesson is not enough. A model-written lesson did not beat re-reading the failed transcript (-1.7 points), self-reflection memory stored the agent's own errors in 22% of annotated cases, and verified or located lessons did better (EDV trap rate 5.0%, Anchor 96.27% vs 73.38% write-all). Retrieval on a failure trigger beat keeping the playbook in context (0.364 vs 0.296 on WebShop).
agent_test: Gate S9 writes behind a check and fetch lessons at the S6 trigger only; test with held-out items and at least 100 items for a 7-point effect.

claim: An external failure layer can change agent behaviour: Sentry paired recovery 33.5% to 60.5% on 200 forks at 1.54x tokens, but an ungated trigger lowered reward (WebShop 0.468 to 0.136 when the need-check was removed) and progress failures (repetition, stall) recovered least (64.0%; 34.0% on SWE-bench Lite). A rule-only baseline gave +52% on WebShop and nothing on AppWorld. No LLM-vs-code detector ablation exists.
agent_test: Measure fire rate, fire step and change rate of the S6 trigger on our traces; compare code-only trigger to LLM trigger.

claim: Reflexion-style lessons have a documented boundary: AlfWorld 130 of 134 tasks in 12 trials, but WebShop showed no gain after 4 trials because the task needs diverse exploration. Lessons do not create strategies the agent never tries.
agent_test: At an impasse require a different operator, not only a note about the failure.
audit_note: Last sentence is an interpretation of Reflexion's own WebShop limitation note; numbers match.

claim: The primary texts for graceful extensibility and the Resilience Assessment Grid remain closed or blocked (Woods 2018 closed access; RAG pages 403). Whether they state testable timing predictions for decompensation is unchecked.
agent_test: None until the texts are opened.
